newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: NSW TO LEGISLATE FOR CHANGED PENALTIES FOR EXTORTION
New South Wales police minister Paul Whelan says he'll legislate to change the penalties for extortion following the threats against Arnotts.
Mr Whelan says the current laws don't cover the entire range or levels of possible extortion offences.
He says he was surprised there'd been no real look at the level of penalties for some time.
Extortionists have threatened to poison Arnotts biscuits unless four New South Wales detective take lie dectors tests over evidence they gave to a 1993 murder trial.
SEARCH CONTINUES FOR NUCLEAR SHIPMENT VESSEL
Greenpeace says improved visibility is likely to give it an easier job of searching for a ship carrying nuclear waste off southern Tasmania.
The organisation resumed it's search this morning for the Pacific Teal, which is thought to be close to entering Australian waters with its shipment of plutonium waste en route to Japan.
Greenpeace Campaigns director, Phyllis Campbell, says the search aircraft will make large grid sweeps, like the ones used in air-sea rescues, to narrow down the search area.
Tasmania's environment minister Peter Hodgman says he'll raise the nuclear waste shipment at a meeting with his state and territory counterparts in Canberra today.
INVESTIGATIONS INTO 3 MINE ACCIDENTS OVERNIGHT
Investigations are underway into three separate mining accidents in the Hunter Valley overnight.
A 45-year-old Toronto man suffered serious injuries when a section of wall collapsed at the Gretley Colliery near Wallsend early today.
He's in a stable condition in Newcastle's John Hunter Hospital.
In an earlier accident at the Cooranbong Colliery near Lake Macquarie, a 27-year-old man suffered head and neck injuries in a rock fall.
And a miner is recovering after suffering pelvic injuries in an accident at Coal and Allied's Hunter Valley Number-One mine near Singleton last night.
District check inspectors from the United Mineworkers Union and officials from the Department of Mineral Resources are investigating the three accidents.
UNION SAYS UP TO 300 ARNOTTS WORKER OFF WORK ON MONDAY
The National Union of Workers says up to 300 permanent staff at the Arnott's factory in Adelaide will have Monday off, while equipment is installed for the company's new, tamper-proof packaging.
Union organiser Bob Hughes says the workers will be taking a day's paid leave.
He says other workers, who are casuals with Arnott's in Adelaide, remain without work, following the extortion threat against the company.
JOINT LEADERS IN SYDNEY GOLF CHALLENGE
New South Wales golfer David Ecob at six under shares the lead in the early stages of the second round of the Canon Golf Challenge at Sydney's Terrey Hills Course.
With an eagle and two birdies to put him at four under for the morning after ten holes, Ecob is six under for the tournament equal with overnight leader Chris Gray who's yet to tee off.
Lucas Parsons and Steve Alker starting the day at five under in equal second spot have both dropped shots - Parsons four under after ten and Alker four under after eight.
Craig Parry who had a bad first round finishing three over birdied the first four holes today to move to one under after nine.
BEVAN AND GILLESPIE IN LINE FOR TEST SPOTS
Spin Bowler Michael Bevan and paceman Jason Gillespie are in line for spots in the first cricket test against South Africa after accounting for seven wickets in the opening day against Natal.
Bevan took three for 56, Gillespie four for 71 with Natal all out for 335 after at one stage being four for 99 at lunch.
In reply the tourists who lost opening bowler Paul Reiffel with a torn hamstring are none for twenty three at stumps - Taylor two - Hayden nine.
